title: IBM Watson Oncology MD Anderson failure
system_purpose: Assist oncologists in identifying suitable cancer treatment options
decision_impact: System recommendations influenced treatment plans for cancer patients at MD Anderson Cancer Center
verified_facts: IBM Watson for Oncology was deployed at MD Anderson Cancer Center from 2013 with a $65 million investment. The pilot program ultimately failed to meet its goals and was discontinued. IBM sold Watson Health in 2022 for $1 billion after originally investing $4 billion in development.
reported_harm: Potential patient harm from incorrect treatment recommendations due to inadequate training data and system limitations for complex oncology cases.
quantitative_evidence: MD Anderson invested $65 million over five years. Watson Health was sold for $1 billion in 2022 after $4 billion investment. No public technical audit of recommendation accuracy is available.
limitations: Public reports describe the failure but no patient-level outcome data is available. The case predates current AI governance frameworks and reflects enterprise software challenges rather than consumer healthcare AI specifically.

title: Racial bias in clinical decision support algorithms
system_purpose: Support clinical decision-making for patient care including triage and resource allocation
decision_impact: Algorithm recommendations influenced care levels and resource allocation affecting patient access to services
verified_facts: Multiple studies documented how clinical decision support algorithms embedded in EHR systems used race as a variable in ways that perpetuated existing healthcare disparities. Historical data used to train models reflected systemic inequities in healthcare delivery.
reported_harm: Delayed or reduced access to appropriate care for minority patients due to algorithmic recommendations based on biased historical data. Examples include algorithms that recommended different care thresholds based on race.
quantitative_evidence: Research from Harvard and NPR documented systemic patterns but specific affected patient counts per algorithm are not publicly available.
limitations: These are documented patterns and research findings rather than specific identified incidents with individual patient harm documentation. Bias can be subtle and difficult to measure without comprehensive demographic data.

title: Chatbot health misinformation and inappropriate triage
system_purpose: Provide health information and triage recommendations to users seeking medical guidance
decision_impact: Chatbot responses influenced user decisions about whether and when to seek medical care
verified_facts: Multiple incidents reported consumer-facing health chatbots providing incorrect information or inappropriate triage guidance. Concerns included over-reliance risk where users trusted automated systems for conditions requiring professional evaluation.
reported_harm: Users may delay appropriate care based on incorrect reassurance from chatbots or may inappropriately seek emergency care based on over-cautious recommendations.
quantitative_evidence: No comprehensive incident database exists; documented cases are individual reports rather than systematic studies.
limitations: Limited publicly available data on specific incidents. Consumer AI health tools are largely unregulated in many markets making comprehensive harm assessment difficult.
